14	ORDER OF THE COMMISSION 
15	Ind. Code ch.  8 -1-26 provides the procedure for the Indiana Utility Regulatory 
16	Commission’s Pipeline Safety Division (“Division”) to find violations of said chapter. Upon 
17	review of those findings, the Indiana Underground Plant Protection Advisory Committee 
18	(“Advisory Committee”) reviews those recommendations and recommends civil penalties in the 
19	Case.   
20	The
21	 Cases received pursuant to Ind.  Code ch. 8-1-26 and ripe for Commission action are 
22	attached hereto and collectively referred to as the Advisory Committee Recommendations.  
23	P
24	ursuant to statute, the Advisory Committee has submitted their recommendations to the 
25	Commission. The Commission UPHOLDS the findings of violations by the Pipeline Safety 
26	Division and APPROVES the recommendations of the Advisory Committee as listed on the 
27	attached pages. The Assistant General Counsel to the Division is directed to prepare and send 
28	notice to the parties advising them of the determination. 
29	Any approved civil penalties are due within 90 days of the date of this Order unless 
30	payment arrangements are made with the Secretary of the Commission.   
31	An
32	y approved trainings must be completed no later than 180 days from  the date of this 
33	Order or the alternative civil penalty noted in the attached recommendation is due.   
34	IT
35	 IS SO ORDERED. 
36	HUSTON, FREEMAN, KREVDA, OBER, AND ZIEGNER CONCUR

39	and correct copy of the Order as approved. 
40	Dana Kosco

AP
PROVED: 
ORDER OF THE COMMISSION 
Ind. Code ch.  8 -1-26 provides the procedure for the Indiana Utility Regulatory 
Commission’s Pipeline Safety Division (“Division”) to find violations of said chapter. Upon 
review of those findings, the Indiana Underground Plant Protection Advisory Committee 
(“Advisory Committee”) reviews those recommendations and recommends civil penalties in the 
Case.   
The
 Cases received pursuant to Ind.  Code ch. 8-1-26 and ripe for Commission action are 
attached hereto and collectively referred to as the Advisory Committee Recommendations.  
P
ursuant to statute, the Advisory Committee has submitted their recommendations to the 
Commission. The Commission UPHOLDS the findings of violations by the Pipeline Safety 
Division and APPROVES the recommendations of the Advisory Committee as listed on the 
attached pages. The Assistant General Counsel to the Division is directed to prepare and send 
notice to the parties advising them of the determination. 
Any approved civil penalties are due within 90 days of the date of this Order unless 
payment arrangements are made with the Secretary of the Commission.   
An
y approved trainings must be completed no later than 180 days from  the date of this 
Order or the alternative civil penalty noted in the attached recommendation is due.   
IT
 IS SO ORDERED. 
HUSTON, FREEMAN, KREVDA, OBER, AND ZIEGNER CONCUR 
APPROVED: 
I hereby certify that the above is a true 
and correct copy of the Order as approved. 
Dana Kosco
Secretary of the Commission

INDIANA CODE CHAPTER 8-1-26.  
)

APPROVED: 
ORDER OF THE COMMISSION 
 Pursuant to India na Code chapte r 8 -1-26, the Pipeline Safety Division (“Division”)  of 
the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission  (“Commission”) investigates excava tion damage 
cases and makes findings violations of said chapter. Upon review of those findings, the Indiana 
Underground Plant  Protection Advisory Committee (“Advisory Committee”) reviews those 
findings and recommends civil penalties in each case.   
Attached to this order are the cases received , with Division findings of violations and 
Advisory Committee recommendations, that are ripe for Commission action.   
The Commission hereby UPHOLDS the findings of violations by the Division and 
APPROVES the recommendations of the Advisory Committee as listed on the attached  pages. 
The Office of General Counsel is directed to prepare and send notice to the parties advising them 
of the determination. 
Civil penalties approved by the Commission are due within 90 days of the date of this 
Order unless payment arrangements are made with the Commission’s Office of General Counsel.  
Trainings approved by the Commission must be completed no later than 90 days from the 
date of this Order unless o therwise agreed in writing by the Commission’s O ffice of General 
Counsel for good cause shown . Failure to complete the training r esults in the alternative civil 
penalty noted in the attached recommendation becoming due.   
IT IS SO ORDERED. 
HUSTON, BENNETT, FREEMAN, VELETA, AND ZIEGNER CONCUR: 
APPROVED: 
I hereby certify that the above is a true 
and correct copy of the Order as approved. 
Dana Kosco 
Secretary of the Commission 
on behalf of

I could not compute either number to a reliable precision, so I have no final answer to give you for 2021 or 2025.

**What I did**

- The text extracts for the 2021 orders (11 files, about 1,600 recommendation forms) and the 2025 orders (10 files, about 1,700 forms) are in `data/text/`. I took the order year from the filenames, which I did not verify against dates inside the orders.
- I pulled the respondent line and the first penalty line for each form. Each form's penalty line starts with "$", "Training", "Warning", or ".5000".
- I have no code-execution tool in this session, so the tallying had to be done by hand. I completed it for one 2021 file only.

**One partial result (not the answer)**

- `ord_PSD_121521.txt` (96 forms): 72 are non-utility. Their headline penalties sum to $189,000, so the mean for that file alone is $189,000 / 72 = **$2,625 per case**. This covers one order, not all of 2021, so it is not the year figure.
- Across that file's non-utility cases, 27 are warning letters ($0) and 31 carry a $5,000 headline, which is why the mean sits so high.

**Estimate**

- For 2021, a rough estimate is in the low-to-mid thousands of dollars per case, and $2,625 from the one file I checked is a reasonable anchor. This is a guess, not a verified figure.
- For 2025, I have no usable estimate. I did not tally the 2025 files.

**What would give an exact answer**

Running a short script over the 2021 and 2025 text files, with the utility-name filter and headline-penalty rules applied, would produce both numbers. Note that some files have blank or wrapped respondent fields (for example, parts of `ord_PSD_122821.txt`), which should be checked when running it. If you can enable a Bash or Python tool, I can do that.
